claim.quote: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 0.20 ppm

key_value_text.quote: a factor of 2 improvement in precision
key_value_text.value: 0.20 ppm precision, a factor of 2 improvement in precision compared to the prior world average

name: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 0.20 ppm

significance.note: This is a precision remeasurement, not framed by the collaboration around a single sigma-significance figure in the material fetched this session; left null rather than guessed.

summary.plain: A second, sharper Fermilab measurement of the same muon property, using over four times as much data as the first result and cutting the experiment's uncertainty in half.
summary.technical: Combines Runs 2 and 3 with Run 1 for more than 4x the positron statistics of the 2021 result and a >50% reduction in systematic uncertainty, reaching 0.20 ppm precision -- a factor-of-2 improvement over the prior world average.

title: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 0.20 ppm
why_it_matters: Tightening the experimental precision on a_mu sharpens the test of the Standard Model and narrows the space for new physics that any discrepancy would imply.
